definitions.gloss: mental concentration; focusing one's mind; composing oneself
definitions.explanation: The act of focusing all mental energy on a single point, clearing distractions. Used in martial arts, sports, meditation, and before important tasks.

examples.japanese: {精神|せいしん}{統一|とういつ}を{図|はか}る。
{試合前|しあいまえ}に{精神|せいしん}{統一|とういつ}して{集中|しゅうちゅう}{力|りょく}を{高|たか}める。
examples.english: I compose my mind before a match to heighten my concentration.

examples.japanese: {弓道|きゅうどう}では{矢|や}を{放|はな}つ{前|まえ}に{精神|せいしん}{統一|とういつ}し、{心|こころ}を{静|しず}めることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: In kyudo (Japanese archery), it is important to focus your mind and calm your heart before releasing the arrow.

notes:
USAGE:
Often associated with martial arts, traditional Japanese arts, and athletic performance. Can also be used humorously when someone is trying to concentrate intensely on an everyday task.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {精神|せいしん}{統一|とういつ}する (to focus one's mind)
- {精神|せいしん}{統一|とういつ}を{図|はか}る (to seek mental composure)
- {精神|せいしん}{統一|とういつ}を{乱|みだ}す (to break one's concentration)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {集中|しゅうちゅう}: concentration — more everyday and general
- {瞑想|めいそう}: meditation — focuses on the practice itself rather than the mental state
